evidence_used: Object image shows a grey fabric-covered case with a woven texture.
Gecko gripper embodiment description requiring flat, smooth, nonporous surfaces for optimal dry adhesion.
Fabric texture introduces micro-roughness and porosity, degrading mushroom-tipped dry-adhesive performance.
calculation_summary: Force estimated via visual heuristic: F = F_base + delta_roughness + delta_weight_guess. Given poor surface compatibility with dry adhesives on woven fabric, adhesive contribution is low, requiring higher normal force to rely on frictional support. Estimated near 5.5 N within the 0 to 8 N range.
assumptions_and_uncertainty: No authoritative mass or friction coefficient was provided.
Visual assessment of fabric porosity and texture is an approximation.
Assumed moderate object weight typical of a portable electronic case.
reasoning_trace: The gecko gripper relies heavily on smooth, flat, nonporous surfaces to maximize van der Waals contact via mushroom-tipped adhesive pads. The visible object surface is covered in a woven textile, which presents micro-roughness and porosity that significantly degrade gecko adhesion. Consequently, dry adhesion is weak, forcing the gripper to rely more heavily on basic frictional support. To compensate for reduced adhesion and ensure a stable lift without slipping, a moderately high normal force of 5.5 N is predicted.
